title: Linking Patterns & Symmetry | Clo Features Deep Dive
description:
Check out this deep dive on all the ways that you can link patterns together in CLO 2025.0! Linking and Symmetry helps you edit and create within CLO faster and more accurately! Check out other new features here: https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Chapters: 
00:00 Intro
00:50 Where to find the Linking Features 
04:28 How each Linking Feature Works 
26:03 Workflows for Linking 
26:40 Simple Workflow 
30:05 Intermediate Workflow 
38:18 Advance Workflow 

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord?utm_campaign=multi_item_banner_JointheOfficialCLODiscord&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=later-linkinbio

---

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/clo-virtual-fashion-inc-/ 
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/clo3d/

markdown_content: ## Linking and Symmetry in Clo: Overview of Core Linking Methods This section explains the four main linking methods in Clo—symmetry, instance patterns, layer clones, and linking to pattern outlines—and where to find these tools primarily within the Transform Pattern Tool and Edit Pattern Tool. Linking means that changes to one element automatically affect another, enhancing workflow efficiency. - **Symmetry** options are accessible via the Transform Pattern Tool and Edit Pattern Tool by right-clicking selected patterns or lines. - **Instance Patterns** create exact copies of patterns linked to the original, found in the Transform Pattern Tool. - **Layer Clones** are linked duplicates layered above or below the original pattern piece, also accessed via right-click in the Transform Pattern Tool. - **Link to Pattern Outline** links internal lines to pattern outlines, enabling coordinated edits between them, available by right-clicking internal lines in the Transform Pattern Tool. - The **Link Line** tool is found in both the Edit Pattern Tool and Edit Sewing Tool, allowing you to link lines or sewing lines to move in coordination. --- ## Symmetry in Clo: Half Symmetry and Full Symmetry Explained This section describes how to apply half and full symmetry within Clo, including procedures for linking pattern points and outlines, and explains their differences with examples. - **Half Symmetry** involves dividing a single pattern piece into two equal halves where one side mirrors the other. Moving a point on one side automatically moves the mirrored point on the other. - Apply via **Transform Pattern Tool** → right-click → *Half Symmetric Pattern*. - Alternatively, use **Edit Pattern Tool** → select edge → right-click → *Unfold Symmetric Editing* (with or without sewing). - Unfolding without linking creates two halves that do not affect each other unless half symmetry is applied. - Half symmetry reduces workload by allowing edits on just one half, with automatic mirroring. - **Full Symmetry** applies between separate pattern pieces that are mirror duplicates. Selecting and moving points on one pattern affects its mirrored counterpart. - Create via **Transform Pattern Tool** → right-click → *Symmetric Pattern* (with or without sewing). - Internal lines linked between symmetric patterns move in coordination with edits. - Clo visually indicates symmetry with a light blue highlight around symmetric pieces and connecting lines between linked patterns. --- ## Instance Patterns and Layer Clones: Definitions and Use Cases This section clarifies the difference between instance patterns and layer clones, their creation methods, and their linking behaviors. - **Instance Patterns** - Exact copies of a pattern piece that remain linked; editing one updates the other identically without mirroring. - Created via **Transform Pattern Tool** → right-click → *Instance Pattern*. - Internal lines move but do not automatically adjust with pattern outline edits. - Instance patterns can be created from half symmetrical patterns, combining linking effects. - Identified by a light green highlight and green connecting lines between linked instance patterns. - **Layer Clones** - Exact copies layered above or below the original, automatically sewn and linked. - Created via **Transform Pattern Tool** → right-click → *Layer Clone Over/Under*. - Editing one pattern piece affects the clone. - Internal lines do not link automatically. - Useful for creating multiple layers of the same pattern (e.g., plackets, facings). - Cloning internal shapes as patterns via right-click does not link them. To link internal shape clones, use the **Trace Tool** with the *Trace as Pattern with Link* function. --- ## Linking Internal Lines to Pattern Outlines This section covers how to link internal lines to pattern outlines to synchronize their edits. - Use **Transform Pattern Tool** → select internal line → right-click → *Link to Pattern Outline*. - After selecting start and end points, the internal line is linked to the pattern outline. - Editing one adjusts the other simultaneously. - To unlink, right-click the linked internal line and choose *Unlink Pattern Outline*, then optimize curves as needed. - Linked internal lines often display additional curve points due to the linkage. --- ## The Linking Tool: Linking Lines and Sewing with Directional Control This section explains the use of the Linking Tool in Clo to link multiple lines or sewing lines, control their movement directions, and manage linked sets. - Access the **Linking Tool** via the **Edit Pattern Tool** or **Edit Sewing Tool** by selecting a line or sewing line → right-click → *Link Lines*. - Visual guidance appears showing arrows indicating the direction each linked line will move relative to others. - Arrows pointing in opposite directions mean lines will move inversely (mirrored). - Arrows pointing the same direction mean lines will move in unison. - You can flip the direction of movement using the right-click option *Flip Direction* or the shortcut **Shift + D**. - Multiple lines can be linked to a single line by holding **Shift** while selecting additional lines before linking. - Linked sewing lines can be managed similarly. - After linking, you can add sewing to the linked lines via right-click *Add Sewing to Linking*. - Unlinking is possible at any time to separate lines as needed. --- ## Practical Workflow Examples: Simple, Intermediate, and Advanced Linking Use Cases This section demonstrates how linking and symmetry features can be applied in practical garment design workflows for efficiency gains. ### Simple Workflow - Apply half symmetry to pattern pieces to link halves, reducing manual edits by half. - Use linked patterns to arrange and sew only half the garment, speeding up 3D window adjustments. - Symmetry allows sewing and arranging with fewer steps, enhancing productivity. ### Intermediate Workflow - Apply half symmetry to collar and other pattern pieces. - Use **Layer Clone Under** to create placket and buttonhole layers that update automatically with the original. - Link internal lines and pattern outlines for components like pockets to maintain consistent edits. - Fold back hems using the Edit Pattern Tool with specified measurements (e.g., half-inch fold). - Link internal lines to pattern outlines in bulk for coordinated editing. - The combination of these techniques streamlines complex garment assembly and fitting steps. ### Advanced Workflow - Address garments with minimal symmetry by creating half symmetry on easily divisible pieces. - Delete unnecessary halves and unfold to create symmetrical pieces. - Link internal lines and pattern outlines strategically to maintain proportional edits across multiple pieces. - Use **Layer Clone Under** selectively for facings or reinforcements. - Employ the Linking Tool to link multiple edges and lines across front and back pieces, ensuring coordinated movement. - Regularly unlink lines after major edits to prevent unintentional cascading changes. - Link internal lines to pattern outlines to maintain consistency in hems or facings. - This approach drastically reduces editing time on complex, asymmetrical garments by leveraging linking and symmetry tools. --- ## Important Tips and Best Practices for Linking in Clo - Always remember to **unlink** lines when you no longer need them linked to avoid unintended edits and messy lines. - Use **half symmetry** as a fundamental linking method to cut editing time significantly. - Combine **instance patterns** and **layer clones** strategically to manage multiple pattern copies efficiently. - Use the **Trace Tool** to create linked patterns from internal shapes, as cloning alone does not link. - Pay attention to directional arrows when linking lines to ensure correct movement behavior. - Linking tools are powerful but require careful management to avoid complex or unintended pattern distortions. - Visual cues such as colored highlights and connecting lines help identify linked patterns and lines quickly. --- This detailed guide on linking patterns and symmetry in Clo equips you with the knowledge to use these features effectively, enabling faster, smarter, and more precise pattern editing workflows.
